title: regex parser spec naming a group the pattern does not define
notes: Fixed (spec docs/error-reporting/specs/E-PARSER.md). Both of the old message's defects are corrected. `in hello` blamed the matched *text*, which had nothing to do with it; the sentence now says the pattern could never have supplied the group whatever the text was. And the group the pattern *does* define is named, which is the whole of the fix: `m.re.groupindex` is a dict on the compiled pattern and `m` is in scope at the raise site, so the list is reachable without touching the AST. Groups are ordered by group number, never by set iteration, so the list cannot move with `PYTHONHASHSEED`. The location is the deepest in the series, `parser.spec.second` at line 5 -- and this is the one entry with a *file* excerpt and a bare `5 |` gutter, both deliberate: nothing about the block's output is relevant, because the error is static, so printing it would repeat the very mistake being fixed; and the offending construct really is in the file at a column `PdlLocationType` has carried since phase-3 item 0. The convention that holds across the series is that a bare `N |` gutter means file lines and a `<label>:N |` gutter means some other text. `_marked_path` guards the descent: a `spec:` written `spec: {object: {...}}` has no mark for `parser.spec.second`, and rather than print a path that is nowhere in the user's file (the E-TYPE-003 defect from INVENTORY 7.9) the walk stops at `parser.spec` and the excerpt is dropped rather than pointed at whatever happens to be on that line. Four `help:` branches, chosen by what the pattern defines: the only group, a `difflib` near miss over an ordered list, a list of the alternatives capped at five, or -- when the pattern has no named group at all -- naming one, or removing `spec:` to get the groups as a list. This reproducer takes the first: `second` against `first` scores well under the 0.7 cutoff, so the near-miss branch does *not* fire, which is exactly the sort of thing a spec gets wrong by assuming and was measured instead. The neighbouring silent failure is untouched and remains open: a `regex:` parser that simply does not match returns `None` and the program prints `null` at exit 0 (INVENTORY 7.10, finding 2). Location 2 -> 3 when `get_loc_string` began rendering `:col`: the header is `prog.pdl:5:5`, the path is `parser.spec.second`, the excerpt is of the file, and the caret sits under `second` at the same column 5 the header names -- the four things rubric item 1 asks for, and the column is the one that was missing. It is the strictest of the three entries that moved, because the caret is under the offending token itself rather than under the construct containing it; there is no `include`/`import`/call chain to add, the failure being in the program that was run.
